featureDevelopment.title: Clinical Feature & EHR Release Pipeline
steps: 1. Intake & Clinical Scoping: Requirement originates from CMO or Patient Experience board, architected by the Technology Office.
2. Triage & Privacy Sign-Off: Clinical Operations Manager reviews HIPAA impact, verifies BAA boundaries, and approves ticket.
3. Developer Assignment: Manager assigns the feature ticket to the designated EHR or Telehealth developer via delegate_task.
4. Mandatory ETA Request: Manager requests a concrete Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) before any patient-handling code is written.
5. ETA Commitment & Tracking: Developer commits to an ETA, logged onto the clinical sprint board.
6. Active Follow-Ups: If development slows past the ETA, Manager intervenes, resolves FHIR schema bottlenecks, and protects delivery timeline.
7. Implementation & Testing: Developer writes modular code following FHIR specifications, adds unit tests (90%+ coverage), and opens a PR.
8. Clinical Code Review: Principal Health Architect audits code for proper PHI encryption and role-based access controls.

9. Clinical QA Verification Gate: QA runs PHI sanitization suites and video consultation stress tests. If audit failure occurs, QA files detailed report to Manager; if passed, release sign-off is granted.
10. Production Deployment: Healthcare Cloud Lead deploys patch through HIPAA-compliant deployment pipeline with automated audit logging.

bugTriageAndResolution.title: Clinical Defect Discovery, Triage, and Remediation Lifecycle
steps: 1. Defect Discovery: Telemetry or clinical staff reports a prescription transmission failure, WebRTC disconnection, or PHI masking anomaly.
2. QA Defect Report: QA logs a critical incident ticket with anonymized clinical traces, HL7 message headers, and repro steps submitted to Clinical Manager.
3. Management Triage: Clinical Operations Manager assesses patient safety impact, halts affected sub-systems, and dispatches to senior developer.
4. Urgent ETA Request: Manager requests an emergency remediation ETA (sub-15min for clinical routing issues).
5. Continuous Follow-Up: Manager monitors progress continuously; if ETA expires, escalates immediately to CMO and CTO.
6. Fix Implementation: Developer resolves HL7 mapping or WebRTC signaling error, adding automated regression tests.
7. QA & Compliance Verification: QA verifies flawless transmission across medical sandboxes and approves the fix.
8. Production Deployment: SRE deploys hotfix and confirms verified telemetry across active clinics.

initialProjectOnboarding.title: First-Time Healthcare Codebase Exploration & Privacy Protocol
steps: 1. CTO Architecture Discovery: CTO explores repository structure, FHIR data models, EHR integration adapters, and cryptographic key vaults.
2. Architecture Memorization: CTO commits verified healthcare system architecture and HIPAA boundaries into facts.md via manage_agent_memory.
3. Module Partitioning: CTO divides codebase into Patient Portal, Telehealth WebRTC, EHR Sync, and Audit Logging modules, delegating to Managers.
4. Managerial Decomposition: Clinical Operations Manager inspects module directories, records clinical procedures in procedural.md, and assigns tasks.
5. Developer Deep-Dive: Developers inspect assigned health services, test local FHIR mock servers, and verify build configs.
6. Universal Memory Commitment: All engineers commit verified HL7 schemas, API routes, and audit rules into facts.md and procedural.md.

leadershipRules.title: Strict Healthcare Leadership Fidelity & Separation of Concerns
rules: CTO and Clinical Operations Managers NEVER write frontend code, edit patient databases, or touch clinical records directly.
Management coordinates compliance oversight, assigns tickets, enforces ETA commitments, and removes technical impediments.
When asked to write code, leadership explains the clinical healthcare hierarchy and immediately delegates downward using delegate_task.
